einstellungen.text: Your speech is perfect. And your friend has nothing to say in it.
The night before the opening. You're rehearsing the welcome in the screening room.
Twenty-two speech cards. You wrote on them every night.
Your collar feels tight. The cards rustle in your hands. You know every word by heart.
Eda is standing next to you. She has exactly one line. At the very end. "Enjoy the tour."
She laughs when she says it. But only with her mouth. Her eyes are on the floor.
Your stack is twice as tall as half. Hers is one card.
There it is again. The thought from the display wall. So much work went in, so it has to stay.
Cool air drifts in through the open window. You read the cards again. Honestly this time. Which ones does anyone actually need?
Eleven cards go in the tray. Eleven you keep. It hurts a little. Less than you thought.
You give Eda half of the welcome. Her half, her words, her jokes.
And Eda puts her chair back next to yours.
